ticket_types.label: VIP / Virtual Server – Not Responding
ticket_types.concept:
VIP issues require comparing the non-working virtual server against a known-working reference. Common root causes:
  1. Pool has no real members or all members are Down/Disabled
  2. Health monitor failure (wrong path, port, expected response)
  3. Missing DNS rewrite in Palo Alto/firewall NAT (internal servers resolve FQDN to public IP)
  4. SNAT pool misconfiguration or missing profiles
  5. SSL profile misconfiguration

Approach: list ltm virtual to compare working vs broken VIP → check pool member states → verify monitor → test DNS resolution from internal host → check firewall NAT for DNS rewrite.
precheck: ! --- List VIP configuration (compare working vs broken) ---
! --- Verify DNS resolution from internal server ---
! Expected: should resolve to SNAT/private IP, not public VIP
prep: ! --- OPTION A: Enable a disabled pool member ---
modify ltm pool <POOL_NAME> members modify { <NODE_IP>:<PORT> { session user-enabled }}
! --- OPTION B: Enable a disabled node ---
! --- OPTION C: Add missing real pool member ---
! --- OPTION D: Create pool with members from scratch ---
! --- OPTION E: Fix DNS rewrite on firewall (Palo Alto) ---
! set rulebase nat rules DST-<VIP_IP> destination-translation dns-rewrite direction forward
rollback: ! --- Disable the member that was enabled ---
modify ltm pool <POOL_NAME> members modify { <NODE_IP>:<PORT> { session user-disabled }}

check.confirm: Customer reports VIP <VIP_IP>:<PORT> (<FQDN>) is not responding. Application behind the VIP is unreachable. Expected behaviour: <EXPECTED_BEHAVIOUR>.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm authorised requester has approved this LTM change.
check.ensure:
! Confirm you are working on the correct F5 device:
show sys version | grep Version
! Cross-reference with Device ID <DEVICE_ID> from ticket

comprehend.what_could_break: Enabling a disabled node may route traffic to an unhealthy server if monitor is not reflecting actual health. Verify monitor status before enabling.
comprehend.expected_result: Pool members will be UP and responding. VIP will distribute traffic correctly. Application will be accessible via <FQDN>.
comprehend.other_teams: Application team should verify application health post-change. Customer to validate end-to-end.

know_before: ! Expected BEFORE: members disabled or dummy pool
know_change: modify ltm pool <POOL_NAME> members modify { <NODE_IP>:<PORT> { session user-enabled }}

ticket_types.label: SSL Certificate – Install / Renew
ticket_types.concept:
SSL certificate renewal on F5 BIG-IP requires a strict sequence to avoid SSL failures:
  1. Install new .crt certificate (no-overwrite preserves old cert for rollback)
  2. Install matching .key private key (must match cert — SSL will fail if mismatch)
  3. Modify client-ssl profile to reference new cert/key/chain
  4. Save sys config
  5. Validate with curl

Critical: install cert and key BEFORE modifying the profile. The no-overwrite flag preserves existing files so rollback only requires a profile modify back to old cert name — no reinstall needed.
precheck: ! --- Identify VIP and its client-ssl profile ---
! Look for 'profiles' section — find client-ssl profile name
! --- Verify old cert and key files exist (for rollback safety) ---
! --- Confirm new cert files are ready ---
prep: ! Install cert → Install key → Modify profile → Save
! --- STEP 1: Install new certificate (no-overwrite = safe rollback) ---
install sys crypto cert <NEW_CERT_NAME>.crt from-editor no-overwrite
! End with a blank line to confirm
install sys crypto key <NEW_CERT_NAME>.key from-editor no-overwrite
! (Paste PEM private key content when prompted)
! --- STEP 3: Update client-ssl profile (CRITICAL — do last) ---
! Expected: correct CN, issuer, updated expiry, HTTP 200
rollback: ! ROLLBACK — Restore previous certificate in ssl profile
! (Old cert/key files preserved by no-overwrite — just repoint profile)

check.confirm: Customer requests SSL certificate renewal on VIP <VIP_IP>:443 (<FQDN>). Current cert <OLD_CERT_NAME> is expiring/expired. New cert <NEW_CERT_NAME> issued by <CA_NAME>. Change to be performed in maintenance window.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm Account Admin has approved this SSL cert change.
! Customer notified before starting work.
check.ensure:
list ltm virtual <VIP_NAME>
list ltm profile client-ssl <SSL_PROFILE_NAME>
! Confirm VIP and SSL profile are correct before making changes.

comprehend.what_could_break: If private key does not match certificate, SSL handshakes will fail causing total HTTPS outage. Rollback plan (restore old cert) is prepared in advance.
comprehend.expected_result: HTTPS VIP will serve new certificate. curl confirms correct CN, issuer, and updated expiry date. No interruption to HTTPS traffic.
comprehend.other_teams: Customer must verify HTTPS access post-change. Browser certificate inspection confirms new cert details.

know_before: ! Note current cert name and expiry
! Note current certificate details in response
know_change: install sys crypto cert <NEW_CERT_NAME>.crt from-editor no-overwrite
install sys crypto key <NEW_CERT_NAME>.key from-editor no-overwrite
modify ltm profile client-ssl <SSL_PROFILE_NAME> replace-all-with { <NEW_CERT_NAME> { cert <NEW_CERT_NAME>.crt key <NEW_CERT_NAME>.key chain <CHAIN_CERT_NAME> } }
know_after: ! Confirm expiry date matches new certificate
! Expected: correct CN = *.<DOMAIN>, issuer = <CA_NAME>, new expiry, HTTP 200

ticket_types.label: Node / Pool Member – Maintenance / Enable-Disable
ticket_types.concept: Node maintenance on F5 requires gracefully removing pool members to avoid dropping active sessions. 'session user-disabled' marks the member as disabled for new connections but allows existing sessions to complete (graceful drain). 'session user-forced-disabled' immediately drops all sessions. Always verify remaining pool members can handle load before disabling any member. Re-enable with 'session user-enabled' after maintenance completes.
precheck: ! --- List all members and their states ---
! --- Check active connections to the node ---
! --- Verify remaining members are UP (ensure load can be absorbed) ---
prep: ! --- DISABLE node for maintenance (graceful — new connections only) ---
modify ltm pool <POOL_NAME> members modify { <NODE_IP>:<PORT> { session user-disabled }}
modify ltm pool <POOL_NAME> members modify { <NODE_IP>:<PORT> { session user-enabled }}
rollback: ! --- Re-enable node if disabled in error ---
modify ltm pool <POOL_NAME> members modify { <NODE_IP>:<PORT> { session user-enabled }}

check.confirm: Customer requests <NODE_IP> (<NODE_NAME>) in pool <POOL_NAME> be <DISABLED/ENABLED> for maintenance. Maintenance window: <WINDOW>.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm authorised requester has approved node maintenance.
check.ensure:
show ltm node <NODE_NAME>
show ltm pool <POOL_NAME>
! Confirm correct node and pool before making changes.

comprehend.what_could_break: Disabling all pool members will make the VIP unavailable. Confirm at least one other member is UP before disabling.
comprehend.expected_result: Node <NODE_NAME> will be marked user-disabled. No new connections will be sent to it. Existing sessions complete normally.
comprehend.other_teams: Application/server team performing maintenance on <NODE_IP> must notify when work is complete so node can be re-enabled.

know_before: ! Note current state of all members
know_after: ! Expected: <NODE_NAME> shows as disabled, other members still UP
